# SPD-028 — A lead's SubagentStop calls a reserved, unbound child never spawned and says spawn it

## Brief
SubagentStop's alive_children already holds a lead once for a child whose spawn PreToolUse(Agent) allowed and never bound, the state SPD-025 adds to Spud's Stop. But alive_children_reason words that child as planned HH:MM and never spawned and tells the lead to spawn it now. That spawn is refused by the reservation, and the refusal names spud --as spud member finish, which the Bash hook refuses inside a subagent, so a lead that follows the words meets two refusals before it reaches spud --as <its agent_id> member finish <child> --status failed. Naming the reservation in the lead's hold (spawn allowed HH:MM, never bound, and no spawn-it-now) and the caller's own actor in hook_agent_spawn's refusal would close it.

Evidence: bin/spud on branch worktree-spd-025-unbound-spawn-stop: alive_children selects planned or active children with no final stop whatever their spawn_requests, and tests/test_hooks.py LeadHoldTest.test_a_reserved_spawn_that_never_bound_is_still_alive shows the hold; alive_children_reason builds 'planned ' + planned_at + ' and never spawned' and 'The planned child never started: spawn it now, or record it with spud --as <agent_id> member finish ... --status failed'; hook_agent_spawn's pending refusal says 'If that spawn failed in the harness, record it with spud --as spud member finish <ref> --status failed' whatever the caller. CLAUDE.md Law 6: the Bash hook refuses --as spud inside a subagent. SPD-025's brief keeps hook_agent_spawn's refusal unchanged, so neither is touched on this branch.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on sonnet, below the persona's opus tier (`--tier-reason`): the change is the wording of two reasons (the lead's SubagentStop hold for a reserved child, and the actor the reservation refusal names) and their tests; which rows hold and which spawns are refused stay as they are. No Fable (Eric, 2026-09-13); no children and no probe. Sequenced after [[SPD-025]]: the engineer starts on a worktree branched from main once SPD-025 is merged (Eric has said to merge it when ready), so the work reuses SPD-025's `reservations` helper and the wording of its unbound clause instead of forking them. Design decided at start: a reserved child in the lead's hold reads "spawn allowed HH:MM (tool_use_id ...), never bound", with no "spawn it now"; its way out is the hook.error check, then `member finish --status failed` under the lead's own agent_id and a new plan. The refusal in `hook_agent_spawn` names the caller's own actor: `--as <agent_id>` for a spudagent, `--as spud` with `[--next]` for Spud's root row. The lead's hold gets no grace period, because a lead's background spawn binds at launch and a foreground one cannot outlive the lead's turn. Spud reads the diff and reruns the suite at return.
